There is no charge for outgoing WebSocket messages, nor for incoming [WebSocket protocol pings ↗︎](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455.5.2) . For compute requests billing-only, a 20:1 ratio is applied to incoming WebSocket messages to factor in smaller messages for real-time communication. For example, 100 WebSocket incoming messages would be charged as 5 requests for billing purposes.

It is recommended to use the WebSocket Hibernation API to avoid incurring duration charges once all event handlers finish running.

## Compute billing examples
* Inactive objects receiving no requests do not incur any duration charges.
* The [WebSocket Hibernation API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/best-practices/websockets/) can dramatically reduce duration-related charges for Durable Objects communicating with clients over the WebSocket protocol, especially if messages are only transmitted occasionally at sparse intervals.
* Pending I/O operations keep an object in memory for up to 15 minutes each. The object incurs duration charges during that time. For more information, refer to [Lifecycle of a Durable Object](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/concepts/durable-object-lifecycle/) .

### Example 1
This example represents a simple Durable Object used as a co-ordination service invoked via HTTP.
* A single Durable Object was called by a Worker 1.5 million times
* It is active for 1,000,000 seconds in the month
In this scenario, the estimated monthly cost would be calculated as:
**Requests** :
* 1.5 million requests - included 1 million requests = 500,000 billable requests.
* (rounded) 1,000,000 requests x $0.15 / 1,000,000 = $0.15.
**Compute Duration** :
* 1,000,000 seconds * 128 MB / 1 GB = 128,000 GB-s.
* 128,000 GB-s is within the 400,000 GB-s included allocation = $0.00.
**Estimated total** : $0.15 (requests) + $0.00 (compute duration) + minimum $5/mo usage = $5.15 per month

### Example 2
This example represents a moderately trafficked Durable Objects based application using WebSockets to broadcast game, chat or real-time user state across connected clients:
* 100 Durable Objects have 50 WebSocket connections established to each of them.
* Clients send approximately one message a minute for eight active hours a day, every day of the month.
In this scenario, the estimated monthly cost would be calculated as:
**Requests** :
* 50 WebSocket connections * 100 Durable Objects to establish the WebSockets = 5,000 connections created each day * 30 days = 150,000 WebSocket connection requests.
* 50 messages per minute * 100 Durable Objects * 60 minutes * 8 hours * 30 days = 72,000,000 WebSocket message requests.
* 150,000 + (72 million requests / 20 for WebSocket message billing ratio) = 3.75 million billing request.
* 3.75 million requests - included 1 million requests = 2,750,000 billable requests.
* (rounded) 3,000,000 requests x $0.15 / 1,000,000 = $0.45.

...

* 100 Durable Objects * 60 seconds * 60 minutes * 8 hours * 30 days = 86,400,000 seconds.
* 86,400,000 seconds * 128 MB / 1 GB = 11,059,200 GB-s.
* 11,059,200 GB-s - included 400,000 GB-s = 10,659,200 GB-s
* (rounded) 11,000,000 GB-s x $12.50 / 1,000,000 = $137.50.
**Estimated total** : $0.45 (requests) + $137.50 (compute duration) + minimum $5/mo usage = $142.95 per month.

...

### Example 3
* 100 Durable Objects each have a single WebSocket connection established to each of them.
* Clients sent one message every second of the month so that the Durable Objects were active for the entire month.
In this scenario, the estimated monthly cost would be calculated as:

content.name: post_message
content.input:
{"text":"Here are the free tiers, checked against vendor pages today (24 Oct 2026).

Supabase Realtime (Free plan): 200 concurrent connections, 2M messages a month, 100 messages a second, 20 presence messages a second, 5 presence calls per client every 30 seconds, 100 channels per connection, and a 256 KB broadcast payload. Presence and broadcast are both included. You get 2 active projects. The main catch is that free projects pause after 7 days of low database activity. Realtime traffic alone may not count as activity, so an idle game could go offline until you resume it in the dashboard. Paid plans start at $25 a month. Sources: supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/limits, supabase.com/pricing, supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/free-project-pausing

Ably (Free package): 200 concurrent connections, 200 concurrent channels, 6M messages a month, 500 messages a second across the account, 200 presence members per channel, 64 KiB per message, and 1 day of message storage. No credit card is needed, there is no time limit, and I found no inactivity pausing. Every message sent and every message delivered counts toward the quota, so fan-out multiplies usage. Going slightly over is tolerated with warnings, then usage gets restricted. Standard costs $29 a month. Sources: ably.com/docs/platform/pricing/free, ably.com/docs/platform/pricing/limits, ably.com/pricing

PartyKit: the hosted platform shut down yesterday (23 Oct 2026). Deploys and room data are gone, and `npx partykit deploy` no longer works. The replacement is PartyServer, which you run on your own Cloudflare account. Source: blog.partykit.io/posts/hosted-platform-shutdown

Cloudflare Workers Free with Durable Objects (what PartyServer runs on): 100,000 requests a day shared with Workers, 10 ms CPU per request, and 13,000 GB-s of Durable Object duration a day. Opening a WebSocket counts as one request. Incoming WebSocket messages are billed at 20 to 1, and outgoing messages are free. Storage is SQLite-only, 5 GB total. Going over a limit makes further operations fail until the 00:00 UTC reset, with no surprise bill. There is no built-in presence; you write it yourself in the room code. No card is needed for Workers Free. Sources: developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing, developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits

What this means for Gotcha, using my own numbers: 6 players sending positions 10 times a second through Ably or Supabase is about 360 messages a second once fan-out is counted. That is above Supabase's 100 a second limit, close to Ably's 500, and would use up Ably's 6M monthly messages in about 4 to 5 hours of play. Either service can handle the lobby, presence, and voice signaling, but positions should go over WebRTC data channels. On Durable Objects, the same traffic comes to about 3 billed requests a second. That fits roughly 9 room-hours a day before the daily request cap, and the duration cap is the tighter limit if the object never gets to hibernate.

Free TURN relays: Metered.ca's free plan gives 500 MB a month, needs no card, and includes free unlimited STUN. Metered's Open Relay gives 20 GB a month, and Metered Realtime adds free signaling with 100 connections and 100k messages a month. Cloudflare Realtime TURN gives 1,000 GB a month of egress free, then $0.05 per GB, and free unlimited STUN at stun.cloudflare.com. Voice only goes through TURN when a direct connection fails, which happens often on mobile carrier networks. One relayed Opus voice stream uses about 20 to 25 MB an hour, so Metered's 500 MB is roughly 20 relayed stream-hours. Sources: metered.ca/pricing, metered.ca/tools/openrelay, developers.cloudflare.com/realtime/turn/faq

Things I could not verify:
1. Commercial use. None of these free-tier pages forbids it. Ably describes its Free package as being for proof-of-concept work but states no ban, and the only explicit "commercial use permitted" claim for Supabase came from a third-party site. I did not read the full terms of service.
2. Whether Cloudflare asks for a card before enabling Realtime TURN on a free account. One user report says some usage-based Cloudflare products do.
3. How reliable Open Relay is.
4. The share of iPhone connections that actually need TURN.

Based on these limits, Cloudflare TURN's 1,000 GB is the strongest free relay. Ably's free tier is the safer pick for the lobby because it never pauses."}

content.name: post_message
content.input:
{"text":"I'm starting on the parts that don't depend on your answers: the city generator, the renderer, gyro look, touch controls, mini-map, HUD, and lobby screens. I'm putting the network code behind a swappable layer, so I can test multiplayer across browser tabs before a real service is chosen. Here's what I need from you:

1. GitHub repo. Please create an empty repo (for example "gotcha") and send me its name. I can't create repos from here.

2. Realtime service. I recommend Supabase Realtime (free tier, needs a Supabase account). It has built-in presence, so the lobby gets "who's here / who left" for free, and it can also carry the voice-chat setup messages. For voice to work reliably on cellular networks it also needs a TURN relay, and I recommend Metered.ca's free tier (needs a second free account). The alternative needs no accounts but is less reliable on cellular: the free public PeerJS server plus direct peer-to-peer connections. Which do you want?

3. Music. I plan to write two original J-Pop-style tracks (lobby and gameplay) that the browser synthesizes as it plays, with no files and no licensing issues. They'll sound like chiptune or synth-pop, not a studio recording. If you'd rather have recorded royalty-free tracks, send them or name a source.

4. Stereo. Your earlier message asked for the left/right split-screen 3D, but this spec doesn't mention it. My plan is a Stereo / Normal toggle, defaulting to Normal, because with the phone held at arm's length and no viewer, most people can't fuse the two halves. Is that right, or should stereo be the default?

5. Action button. What should it do? My guess is "pick up an item within reach", so items aren't collected just by walking through them. I can also make it a skateboard trick or a wave to other players.

6. "Who has yet to join". The host only knows about players who have joined. Should the host enter an expected player count or a list of names, so the lobby can show the empty slots? I'm assuming an optional expected count.

Unless you say otherwise, I'm also assuming everyone starts from the same point, with a maximum of 8 players. 8 is about the limit for direct voice connections between every pair of phones."}

- **Message rate:** 500 messages per second
- **Messages:** 6,000,000 per month
- **Channels:** 200 concurrent channels
- **Connections:** 200 concurrent connections. The page doesn't use the term "peak," so this is the closest match to your "peak connections" item.
- **Credit card:** Not required. The page states "No credit card is required to sign up."

According to the changelog, Durable Objects are available on the Workers Free plan with "zero commitment."

**What the free tier includes:**
- Use of Durable Objects for AI agents (via the Agents SDK), collaboration tools, and real-time apps like chat or multiplayer games.
- A SQLite database for each Durable Object, accessed through the Storage API.
- The ability for every Worker request to call a Durable Object.

**Limits:**
- Free plan limits apply to Durable Object compute and storage usage.
- The page doesn't list specific numbers. It refers to the Durable Objects pricing page for those details.

The page doesn't say whether the managed platform is free. It only states that "The PartyKit platform fee is free for cloud-prem deployments." Also, the hosted platform is shutting down, with deploys stopping on 16 October and the platform shutting down on 23 October 2026.

To deploy to your own Cloudflare account (cloud-prem), you need:

- **Your Cloudflare account ID**, set as `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
- **A Cloudflare API token**, created with the "Edit Cloudflare Workers" template, set as `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`.
- **A domain**, passed with `--domain` or set as `domain` in `partykit.json`.

You then run `npx partykit deploy` with those values. The page also warns that this method stops working on 23 October 2026, and recommends PartyServer with `wrangler` for new projects.

The notice says the ban on performances and singing was lifted effective June 22, 2026, limited to social media posts such as YouTube and TikTok. It refers readers to the License and FAQ on dova-s.jp for the "scope of use, prohibited activities" and other details.

content.input: {"prompt":"Quote exactly the clauses on: commercial use, credit, use in games or web applications, redistribution of the audio files, and whether hosting the file inside a public website/game (extractable) is allowed. Also any per-track composer-specific restrictions.","url":"https://opentracks.com/en/help/articles/license/"}

content:
**Commercial use**
Scope of the License, item 1 says users may use the audio sources "whether commercial/non-commercial and individual/corporate," subject to this License and any composer conditions.

**Credit**
Preconditions, item 2 states: "Users are not required to display copyright notices or credits when using the audio sources."

**Use in games or web applications**
- Background music examples include "Use in paid or free products/works (games, DVDs, etc.)."
- The page also lists "Use in paid or free apps (iPhone, Android, etc.) and web services," but adds that the License "does not apply to tool apps or platforms." For embedding in tool apps or platforms, it says to "consult site management in advance."

**Redistribution of audio files**
Prohibited Uses, item 7 prohibits "Distributing or selling the audio sources." A note under it says this covers any method that "allows end users to use the audio source alone, regardless of format."

**Hosting files in a public website or game (extractable)**
Prohibited Uses, item 8 prohibits "Using audio sources in a state where end users can easily access and duplicate the audio files as audio files without conversion."

**Per-track composer restrictions**
Preconditions, item 3 says composers "may impose separate usage conditions," and that "the composer/creator's conditions take precedence" for matters not otherwise specified. However, the preconditions on credit and royalties and the Prohibited Uses still take precedence over composer conditions. The page does not list any specific per-track restrictions, so those would need to be checked on each track's own page.

import struct,zlib
# simple 180x180 PNG gradient icon placeholder
w=h=180
rows=[]
for y in range(h):
  r=b'\x00'
  for x in range(w):
    t=(x+y)/(2*w)
    c1=(0xa9,0xd6,0xf5);c2=(0x5f,0xbf,0xb4);c3=(0xff,0xa6,0x6b)
    if t<.55: a,b,k=c1,c2,t/.55

    elif d<36: col=[0xff,0xf6,0xc9]

  rows.append(r)
raw=b''.join(rows)
def chunk(t,d): return struct.pack('>I',len(d))+t+d+struct.pack('>I',zlib.crc32(t+d)&0xffffffff)

open('icon-180.png','wb').write(png)
"

{"text":"Yes. This is side-by-side stereo rendering. A browser game built with WebGL (for example Three.js) can render the scene twice per frame from two cameras set about 6.3 cm apart, putting the left view on the left half and the right view on the right half. It works from a plain URL with nothing to install.

Two points decide whether it works well:
1. Viewing method. On a phone in a Cardboard-style viewer, or with parallel free-viewing, the left image goes on the left. Cross-eye viewing needs the halves swapped. Parallel free-viewing without a viewer only works on small images, because each half can be no wider than the distance between your eyes.
2. Device. A phone in a headset can also use the gyroscope for head tracking. On a desktop monitor, comfortable viewing without a viewer is limited.

Tell me which viewing method and device you have in mind, plus a game idea if you have one, and I'll start building."}

**Audit findings**

1. "Integration Webhooks" (4201909) calls SwitchBot only. No Beds24 call exists anywhere in Make. The SwitchBot Bearer token is hardcoded in the header — that's the only API credential Make has.

2. "Beds24 → Claude Router" (8127391) is a skeleton: it fires a Claude Code trigger URL with placeholder token and trigger_id. Never wired up, 0 executions. Useful as a callback path once we fill in real values.

3. Make has no Beds24 credentials. Any Beds24 call from Make would require storing the refreshToken somewhere in Make and doing a 2-step auth (refreshToken → token → call). That's complex and puts the refreshToken in Make.

4. `1.pin` in "Integration Webhooks" IS the keyId. The PIN sent at booking time = last 6 of bookingId = what SwitchBot fires as `context.keyId` on check-in. They're the same number.

5. Full bookingId is NOT available in "Integration Webhooks". The webhook only carries `pin, guest, checkin, checkout, device_id`. To get bookingId we need Beds24 lookup, which works from Claude Code (proxy injects token) but not cleanly from Make.

6. `floor()` is confirmed in use in "Integration Webhooks". Make's formula docs also include `mod(a, b)` — modulo is available.

**Proposed architecture**

Step A — "Integration Webhooks" addition (Make):
Add one `datastore:AddRecord` module at the end. Cache: `{key: 1.pin, guest: 1.guest, deviceMac: first(split(1.device_id, ",")), checkin: 1.checkin, checkout: 1.checkout}` in a new data store "Guest Key Map". This runs at PIN creation (2 days before check-in), so it's ready when the guest arrives.

Step B — Scenario 8131103 redesign (Make):
On check-in webhook: lookup "Guest Key Map" by keyId → get guest_name (no Beds24 needed). Then ExistRecord check → AddRecord to data store 229823. Then fire a signal to Claude Code via the "Beds24 → Claude Router" webhook (fill in real trigger URL + token).

Step C — Claude Code trigger (every ~10 min):
Reads data store 229823 for check-ins since last run. For each: finds Beds24 bookingId via `mod(bookingId, 1000000) == keyId` on current bookings (uses proxy auth, no Make credential needed). Writes CHECKIN info item to Beds24. Updates ArtifactData `stays` with `checkedIn: true`.

Step D — Board HTML:
In `stayBlock()`, when `s.checkedIn === true` change `border-left` to use `var(--ok)` (green).

**What needs your approval before I build:**

1. Modifying "Integration Webhooks" (active production scenario) to add the data store cache step.
2. Writing CHECKIN info items to Beds24 from the Claude Code trigger — this is a Beds24 write, outside the weekly rate/availability batch category. You asked for it earlier but I want explicit confirmation before touching Beds24 data.
3. The 10-minute polling interval is acceptable for "near real-time."

If you approve all three, I'll build in this order: Step A → Step B → Step D → Step C (board visible before CRON is live).

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Check-in sync: reads Make data store for SwitchBot check-ins,
writes CHECKIN info items to Beds24, updates ArtifactData board.
Runs every ~10 minutes via CRON trigger.
"""
import os
import sys
import json
import time
import urllib.request
import urllib.error
from datetime import datetime, timezone

BEDS24_BASE = "https://beds24.com/api/v2"
MAKE_DS_ID = 229823
MAKE_BASE = "https://eu1.make.com/api/v2"
ARTIFACT_ID = "GeFRLVdrhqj2CnkyHzw4bu"
UNIT_NAMES = {"101": "101", "201": "201", "301": "301"}

def beds24_request(method, path, body=None):
    url = f"{BEDS24_BASE}{path}"
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json"}
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read())

def make_request(method, path, body=None):
    make_token = os.environ.get("MAKE_API_TOKEN")
    if not make_token:
        raise RuntimeError("MAKE_API_TOKEN not set")
    url = f"{MAKE_BASE}{path}"
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Accept": "application/json",
        "Authorization": f"Token {make_token}",
    }
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read())

def get_checkin_records():
    """Fetch all records from data store; return those with checked_in_at > 0 and no map_ prefix."""
    records = []
    page = 1
    while True:
        resp = make_request("GET", f"/data-stores/{MAKE_DS_ID}/data?pg={page}&pgSize=100")
        items = resp.get("dataStoreData", [])
        for item in items:
            key = item.get("key", "")
            # check-in dedup records: format is {deviceMac}_{keyId}, not map_...
            if key.startswith("map_"):
                continue
            data = item.get("data", {})
            checked_in_at = data.get("checked_in_at", 0)
            if checked_in_at and checked_in_at > 0:
                records.append({
                    "key": key,
                    "key_id": data.get("key_id", ""),
                    "unit": data.get("unit", ""),
                    "guest_name": data.get("guest_name", ""),
                    "device_mac": data.get("device_mac", ""),
                    "checked_in_at": checked_in_at,
                })
        if len(items) < 100:
            break
        page += 1
    return records

def find_booking_by_key_id(key_id):
    """Find Beds24 bookingId where bookingId % 1000000 == int(key_id)."""
    key_id_int = int(key_id)
    today = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    # Fetch bookings with arrival within ±30 days
    resp = beds24_request("GET", f"/bookings?arrivalFrom=2026-01-01&arrivalTo=2027-12-31&status=1")
    bookings = resp.get("data", [])
    for booking in bookings:
        bid = booking.get("id", 0)
        if bid % 1000000 == key_id_int:
            return booking
    return None

def write_checkin_to_beds24(booking_id, checked_in_at):
    """Write CHECKIN info item to Beds24 booking."""
    checkin_time = datetime.fromtimestamp(checked_in_at / 1000, tz=timezone.utc)
    jst_offset = 9 * 3600
    checkin_jst = datetime.fromtimestamp(checked_in_at / 1000 + jst_offset, tz=timezone.utc)
    text = checkin_jst.strftime("Checked in via SwitchBot at %Y-%m-%d %H:%M JST")
    payload = [{"id": booking_id, "infoItems": [{"code": "CHECKIN", "text": text}]}]
    resp = beds24_request("POST", "/bookings", payload)
    return resp

def get_artifact_data_stays():
    """Read stays collection from ArtifactData — done via Claude Code SDK call."""
    # ArtifactData is only accessible via the Artifact tool in Claude Code sessions.
    # This script runs in a CRON trigger context: we use the beds24 proxy to update
    # stays via ArtifactData through the MCP tool pathway.
    # For the CRON context, we write a signal file that the Claude Code session picks up.
    # Since ArtifactData can only be called from within a Claude Code turn, we instead
    # write to a signal file that the trigger script reads and calls ArtifactData.
    pass

def write_signal(record):
    """Write a signal file for the trigger handler to pick up and call ArtifactData."""
    signals_dir = "/mnt/project-files/checkin_signals"
    os.makedirs(signals_dir, exist_ok=True)
    fname = f"{signals_dir}/{record['key']}.json"
    if not os.path.exists(fname):
        with open(fname, "w") as f:
            json.dump(record, f)
        return True
    return False

def main():
    print(f"[{datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}] checkin_sync starting")
    records = get_checkin_records()
    print(f"  Found {len(records)} check-in records")

    for rec in records:
        key_id = rec["key_id"]
        unit = rec["unit"]
        checked_in_at = rec["checked_in_at"]

        print(f"  Processing unit={unit} key_id={key_id} checked_in_at={checked_in_at}")

        # Find Beds24 booking
        booking = find_booking_by_key_id(key_id)
        if not booking:
            print(f"    WARNING: no booking found for key_id={key_id}")
            continue

        booking_id = booking["id"]
        print(f"    Matched bookingId={booking_id}")

        # Write CHECKIN to Beds24
        try:
            resp = write_checkin_to_beds24(booking_id, checked_in_at)
            print(f"    Beds24 CHECKIN written: {resp}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"    ERROR writing Beds24 CHECKIN: {e}")

        # Signal for ArtifactData update
        new_signal = write_signal({
            "key": rec["key"],
            "unit": unit,
            "key_id": key_id,
            "booking_id": booking_id,
            "checked_in_at": checked_in_at,
            "guest_name": rec["guest_name"],
        })
        if new_signal:
            print(f"    Signal written for ArtifactData update")
        else:
            print(f"    Signal already exists (ArtifactData already updated)")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

{"id":"main","data":{"sections":[{"text":"Run Crest House, a three-apartment small hotel in Nakano-ku, Tokyo (units 101, 201, 301), as a solo operator with Claude as COO, so that nothing about a guest, cleaner, vendor, legal requirement or payment is missed. Bookings come from Airbnb (about 80%) and Booking.com (about 20%); Agoda and VRBO are to be added.\nDone each day: every arrival in the next 14 days has a cleaned unit, a known arrival time, special requests arranged and a completed guest registry (legally required for every guest, including children); every cleaning is assigned and confirmed the day before with the next guest's arrival time and party size; every guest, vendor and cleaner message has a reply drafted (native Japanese with an English translation where needed); Vi has one short, prioritised list for the day with drafts ready to copy.\nRunning targets, to confirm with Vi: books closed in Money Forward each month; mailbox kept manageable; door codes and registry links made harder to guess; Agoda and VRBO live.","title":"Goal"},{"text":"Vi (Vincci Kumabe, 隈部ヴィンシ) runs Crest House solo through SpoonBike株式会社: 3 apartments (101, 201, 301) plus a garage and a B1 rainwater pit in Nakano-ku, Tokyo. Bookings: about 80% Airbnb, 20% Booking.com; Agoda and VRBO are planned. Vi does not speak Japanese, has ADHD and is disorganised, so every output is short, prioritised, one next action. Claude acts as COO (daily brief, board, coordination) with specialist threads for cleaners, guests, vendors and property, CFO (Money Forward Cloud) and inbox cleanup.","title":"Who and what"},{"text":"Neutral, factual, trustworthy. No flattery, hype, enthusiasm, emotional or supportive commentary, no closing reassurance. Say plainly when something is unknown. State a weak plan once. Plain text in chat, no markdown headers. Create no documents or files unless Vi asks (the board is the exception). Japanese must be native-quality, always followed by an English back-translation. Never send, post, pay or change anything in any system: draft and report only. Systems are read-only unless Vi explicitly approves a specific change. Never put guest-nationality generalisations in any message or policy.","title":"Rules for Claude"},{"text":"Beds24 is the channel manager; read-only API through Carly (key stored there, never typed in chat). Guest registry: https://guestregistry.cresthouse.jp/?bookingId=[Beds24 booking id], the Lovable project Japan Guest Pass (Supabase, table guest_registrations; read counts only, never passport, address, birth date, phone, email or names). The Lovable project Guest Connect Pass is NOT the live registry. Money Forward Cloud is connected for the CFO thread. Its tools include write functions (post and put for journals, transactions, trade partners, journal rules): Claude uses only the read tools unless Vi explicitly instructs a specific write in the CFO thread. Gmail connector for mail. LINE is not readable: Vi pastes cleaner messages into the Notes box on the board or into a thread.","title":"Systems"},{"text":"北村 (Kitamura): Japanese; Vi's on-site contact with 小川商会 for drain work; 石戸 has criticised her tidiness, never repeat that to her or him. 石戸 (Ishido): address as 石戸さん; short polite です/ます (more formal いたします when asked); has a main job and other properties so some days he is only free from the afternoon; invoices twice a month (first half, second half) and Vi pays by bank transfer; extra time is paid at HIS discretion on his invoice, never capped; dislikes short notice, being kept waiting, and anything that sounds like blame; give notice early, apologise plainly for the specific inconvenience, say what is changing and why; avoid the ambiguous 大丈夫 and 結構です (use explicit wording such as ...でお願いします or ...はなしにします). 野村 (Nomura): new, first clean 10/21, not yet confirmed. Genelyn: English. Vi sends all LINE messages herself. Each day Claude drafts the reconfirmation for the next day's clean: confirm the clean, give the next guest's arrival time ('unconfirmed' if unknown) and number of guests (adults + children) so towels and amenities are right, plus extra tasks.","title":"Cleaners"},{"text":"Check-in is self-service by door code, standard from 15:00; check-out 10:00. Vi writes to guests as 'Vi' in a friendly native-Canadian English voice (other languages written as a native host would, not translated). Beds24 auto actions send: welcome with registry link, door code about three days before arrival, a 24-hour registration reminder, and a multilingual check-out reminder (EN, JA, KO, ZH-S, ZH-T; the Japanese one is deliberately shorter). The registry is legally required for every guest including children (one passport per guest). A booking counts as registered when guest_registrations rows >= adults + children. When a party sends passports by message, Vi enters them by hand and the board shows 'passports sent by message' until she does. Special requests Vi wants to know about in advance: early check-in, late check-out, luggage storage, high chair, baby cot, airport transfer, child ages.","title":"Guests"},{"text":"小川商会 (Ogawa Shokai): 立神 (Tatsugami, maintenance; mente-cyosui@ogawa-syoukai.co.jp, m_katagami@ogawa-syoukai.co.jp) for drain and pit cleaning; 野老 (Tokoro, recycling; recycle-05@ogawa-syoukai.co.jp) for waste collection and bulky items (suitcases from ¥2,000). Drain quote (ex tax): high-pressure cleaning ¥95,000 with endoscope and toilet removal, or ¥65,000 without removing toilets; B1 pit cleaning ¥44,000 (vacuum truck) or ¥15,000 (simple vacuum). Work moved from 10/22 to proposed 10/25, Vi emailed 立神; reply and final quote outstanding. すっきりマイスター (山田) does aircon and house cleaning. Open property items from 石戸's 10/8 report: possible rodent entry in the storage by the stairs, wallpaper peeling at the 201 bathroom sink, toilet paper and guest chocolates restock, soiled-pillow and makeup covers too few and not distinguishable, leaves over the public road.","title":"Vendors and property"},{"text":"Beds24 Japanese auto message sent with the literal [GUESTLASTNAME] (booking 94926483) and an English guest received a Japanese message: check tag name and language filter. Door PIN is the last six digits of the Beds24 booking id and the registry link needs only the booking id (shows guest name, dates and unit): both guessable, Vi has been told. Beds24 does not show some replies Vi sends on the OTA apps.","title":"Known issues"},{"text":"No early check-in for Matt Chenoy (10/31); Robert Burns arrives 15:00 (early check-in declined). 201 on 10/30 is 石戸 only; 201 on 10/31 is Genelyn. Drain work moved to proposed 10/25. 石戸's 10/22 toilet check is superseded and he must be told (open). 101 after Wyatt on 10/25 has no cleaner (open). Wyatt Chism booked 101 for 10/22-10/25 on 10/19. 2026-10-20: reschedule email to 立神 drafted (10/22 to 10/25), reply and final quote outstanding; Indie (Amanda's party) sent four passports by message, Vi enters them by hand; Wyatt Chism's booking has a guest comment not yet read.","title":"Decisions so far"},{"text":"The Crest House Board (https://claude.ai/artifact/GeFRLVdrhqj2CnkyHzw4bu) is the shared memory: tasks, stays, cleans, waiting, flags, notes, this playbook. Vi edits it directly and Vi's edits win (marked by:'vi'); the morning run never overwrites them. The 7:59 Tokyo routine fires INTO the COO thread (a thread that holds the Gmail, Carly and Lovable connectors), refreshes the board and posts a short summary. A routine that starts a brand-new session each run does NOT get those connectors (tested 20 Oct 2026: only the board was readable), so do not switch to that. Threads: COO (daily brief and coordination), Cleaners and turnovers, Guests and requests, Vendors and property, CFO, Inbox cleanup. Claude only learns of board changes when it reads the board (each morning and at the start of each reply in the COO thread). Reset the COO thread weekly or near 850,000 tokens: update this playbook, create a new COO thread with create_session (threads created that way get the connectors), create a routine with create_trigger bound to it (persistent_session_id), disable the old routine, tell Vi where to continue.","title":"How the system works"}],"updated":"Tue 20 Oct 2026, revised"},"version":2,"updatedAt":"2026-10-20T09:18:37.067312Z"}
